source.title: The ECHELON-2 Trial: 5-year results of a randomized, phase III study of brentuximab vedotin with chemotherapy for CD30-positive peripheral T-cell lymphoma
source.source_type: 5-year exploratory follow-up of a randomized, double-blind, phase III active-comparator trial
source.design: double-blind, double-dummy, randomized, placebo-controlled, active-comparator phase III trial

extraction_metadata.scope_note: The primary article and five supplied supplements were inspected as one source packet. Bibliographic entries were not atomized. The 5-year analysis is preserved as exploratory and nominal where the source says so. All model-extracted atoms remain needs_review pending independent human verification.

atoms.canonical_statement: The 5-year ECHELON-2 update evaluated long-term progression-free survival, overall survival, prespecified subgroup outcomes, response to subsequent brentuximab vedotin, and peripheral neuropathy resolution or improvement.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: PFS per investigator and OS in the intent-to-treat (ITT) population, results in prespecified subgroups, response rates with brentuximab vedotin treatment after frontline therapy, and peripheral neuropathy (PN) resolution and improvement.

atoms.canonical_statement: ECHELON-2 was a double-blind, double-dummy, randomized, placebo-controlled, active-comparator phase III trial.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: ECHELON-2 is a double-blind, double-dummy, randomized, placebo-controlled, active-comparator phase III study.

atoms.canonical_statement: ECHELON-2 was registered as NCT01777152.
Eligible patients were at least 18 years old.
Eligible patients had an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 2 or less.

Eligible patients had previously untreated CD30-positive peripheral T-cell lymphoma with CD30 detected in at least 10% of neoplastic cells by local review; total lymphocytes were used when neoplastic cells could not be enumerated.

Eligible histologies included ALK-positive systemic anaplastic large cell lymphoma with IPI at least 2, ALK-negative systemic anaplastic large cell lymphoma, PTCL-NOS, AITL, adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma, enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma, and hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma.
Enrollment targeted 75% plus or minus 5% systemic anaplastic large cell lymphoma to satisfy European and Canadian regulatory requirements.
Patients assigned to A+CHP received six or eight 21-day cycles of brentuximab vedotin, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, and prednisone.
Patients assigned to CHOP received six or eight 21-day cycles of cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone.
Consolidative autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation or radiotherapy was permitted after frontline treatment at investigator discretion, with transplant intent specified before cycle 1.

The primary progression-free survival endpoint was time from randomization to first relapse or progressive disease, death from any cause, or subsequent systemic chemotherapy for residual or progressive PTCL, whichever occurred first.

outcome.definition: time from randomization to relapse/progression, death from any cause, or subsequent systemic chemotherapy for residual/progressive PTCL, whichever occurred first

atoms.canonical_statement: Overall survival was a key alpha-controlled secondary endpoint.
Complete remission rate and objective response rate were key alpha-controlled secondary endpoints.
Long-term computed tomography scans were required at months 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, and 24 and every 6 months thereafter until progression, death, or primary-endpoint analysis.
The relationship between local CD30 expression above or below the subtype median and complete remission or objective response was assessed post hoc in AITL and PTCL-NOS patients treated with A+CHP.
Adverse events were coded with MedDRA version 21.0 and graded with NCI CTCAE version 4.03; peripheral neuropathy resolution and improvement were monitored in extended follow-up.
The 5-year analysis used a 5 November 2020 data cutoff, Kaplan-Meier estimation for PFS, and a stratified Cox proportional hazards model with histology and baseline IPI strata.
Efficacy analyses used the intent-to-treat population, while safety analyses included patients who received any study treatment.
The 5-year update was exploratory and was not prespecified in the protocol; PFS was assessed by investigators after the blinded independent central reader closed following the primary analysis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This update at 5 years is exploratory as it was not prespecified in the protocol.

atoms.canonical_statement: P values in the 5-year analysis were nominal and were not adjusted for multiplicity.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: P values are nominal and not adjusted for multiplicity.

atoms.canonical_statement: From 24 January 2013 through 7 November 2016, 452 patients in 17 countries were randomized 1:1 to A+CHP or CHOP, 226 per arm, and follow-up to last contact had a median of 66.8 months with a range of 0 to 90 months.
Of 452 randomized patients, 124 (27%) had stage III disease and 240 (53%) had stage IV disease.
Of 452 randomized patients, 351 (78%) had an IPI score of at least 2.
Systemic anaplastic large cell lymphoma accounted for 316 of 452 patients (70%), including 218 (48%) with ALK-negative disease and 98 (22%) with ALK-positive disease.
Only patients with IPI score at least 2 were enrolled in the ALK-positive systemic anaplastic large cell lymphoma subgroup.
The CONSORT diagram reports 601 screened individuals and 452 randomized patients; three patients randomized to A+CHP did not receive study treatment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Includes three subjects who were randomized to the A+CHP arm but did not receive study treatment.

atoms.canonical_statement: A+CHP reduced the hazard of a progression-free survival event versus CHOP with HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.53 to 0.91; P=0.0077).
Median progression-free survival was 62.3 months with A+CHP and 23.8 months with CHOP.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: median PFS in A+CHP arm, months
quantitative_result.original_result_text: A+CHP 62.3 months (95% CI 42.0 months to not evaluable); CHOP 23.8 months (95% CI 13.6-60.8 months).

atoms.canonical_statement: Estimated 5-year progression-free survival was 51.4% with A+CHP and 43.0% with CHOP.
In systemic anaplastic large cell lymphoma, the PFS hazard ratio for A+CHP versus CHOP was 0.55 (95% CI 0.39 to 0.79; P=0.0009).
In systemic anaplastic large cell lymphoma, estimated 5-year PFS was 60.6% with A+CHP and 48.4% with CHOP.
In AITL, estimated 5-year PFS was 26.6% with A+CHP and 48.1% with CHOP.
In PTCL-NOS, estimated 5-year PFS was 26.5% with A+CHP and 25.7% with CHOP.
A+CHP reduced the hazard of death versus CHOP with HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.53 to 0.99; P=0.0424).
Estimated 5-year overall survival was 70.1% with A+CHP and 61.0% with CHOP.
In systemic anaplastic large cell lymphoma, the OS hazard ratio for A+CHP versus CHOP was 0.66 (95% CI 0.43 to 1.01; P=0.0529).
In systemic anaplastic large cell lymphoma, estimated 5-year OS was 75.8% with A+CHP and 68.7% with CHOP.
In AITL, estimated 5-year OS was 67.8% with A+CHP and 62.5% with CHOP.
In PTCL-NOS, estimated 5-year OS was 46.2% with A+CHP and 35.9% with CHOP.
In patients aged 65 years or older, the PFS hazard ratio for A+CHP versus CHOP was 0.68 (95% CI 0.45 to 1.04).
In patients aged 65 years or older, the OS hazard ratio for A+CHP versus CHOP was 0.62 (95% CI 0.39 to 0.98).
In women, the PFS hazard ratio for A+CHP versus CHOP was 0.44 (95% CI 0.28 to 0.69).
In non-sALCL histologies, the PFS hazard ratio for A+CHP versus CHOP was 0.96 (95% CI 0.63 to 1.47).
In AITL, the PFS hazard ratio for A+CHP versus CHOP was 1.41 (95% CI 0.64 to 3.11).
In PTCL-NOS, the PFS hazard ratio for A+CHP versus CHOP was 0.79 (95% CI 0.43 to 1.43).
Among AITL patients, 26 of 29 (90%) had CD30 expression between 10% and 30%, with a median expression of 18%.

atoms.canonical_statement: In AITL patients treated with A+CHP, complete remission occurred in 8 of 14 patients (57%) with CD30 above the median and 8 of 15 (53%) with CD30 at or below the median; the comparison P value was 0.84.

atoms.canonical_statement: Within the trial-eligible CD30 range, the investigators found no apparent correlation between CD30 expression above or below the subtype median and complete remission in AITL or PTCL-NOS, and responses occurred across the observed CD30 range.
The CD30 response analysis was exploratory and post hoc and was not powered to detect an effect of CD30 expression on response likelihood.
Because ECHELON-2 required CD30 expression of at least 10%, the trial does not establish A+CHP efficacy in patients with absent or lower CD30 expression.
Consolidative stem-cell transplantation was reported in 50 of 226 A+CHP patients (22%) and 39 of 226 CHOP patients (17%).
Overall stem-cell transplantation use was 68 of 226 (30%) with A+CHP and 64 of 226 (28%) with CHOP.
Stem-cell transplantation as subsequent therapy was reported in 23 of 226 A+CHP patients (10%) and 31 of 226 CHOP patients (14%).
Subsequent brentuximab vedotin monotherapy was used in 24 of 226 A+CHP patients (11%) and 47 of 226 CHOP patients (21%).

atoms.canonical_statement: The first subsequent therapy produced an objective response rate of 42% in both frontline arms; complete remission rates were 27% after A+CHP and 19% after CHOP.

Median time from frontline therapy to brentuximab vedotin retreatment or treatment was 15.0 months after A+CHP and 8.2 months after CHOP.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors interpreted the retreatment findings as supporting brentuximab vedotin retreatment as a viable option after relapse.
The brentuximab vedotin retreatment analysis involved small patient numbers and investigator-assessed responses and was descriptive rather than a randomized comparison.
Peripheral neuropathy was reported in 117 of 226 A+CHP patients (52%) and 124 of 226 CHOP patients (55%).
At last follow-up, ongoing peripheral neuropathy was reported in 47 of 226 A+CHP patients (21%) and 42 of 226 CHOP patients (19%).
Peripheral neuropathy improved or resolved in 84 of 117 affected A+CHP patients (72%) and 97 of 124 affected CHOP patients (78%).

quantitative_result.effect_measure: A+CHP improvement or resolution among PN cases (%)

atoms.canonical_statement: Assessment of grade 2 or 3 peripheral neuropathy outcomes was confounded in 19 of 29 patients by death in 12, study withdrawal in 6, and loss to follow-up in 1.
Secondary malignancies were reported in 14 patients, 6 in the A+CHP arm and 8 in the CHOP arm.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: secondary malignancy count in A+CHP arm

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that A+CHP continued to provide clinically meaningful PFS and OS improvement over CHOP at 5 years in CD30-positive PTCL.
The authors highlighted ongoing remission in more than 60% of systemic anaplastic large cell lymphoma patients at 5 years with A+CHP.
The authors described the long-term safety profile as manageable, including continued resolution or improvement of peripheral neuropathy.
The study intentionally enrolled a high proportion of systemic anaplastic large cell lymphoma and was not powered to compare A+CHP with CHOP within non-ALCL histologic subtypes.
The work was funded by Seagen Inc. and Millennium Pharmaceuticals, a Takeda subsidiary, and in part by NIH/NCI Cancer Center grant P30 CA008748.
Medical writing assistance was funded by Seagen Inc.

The article reports extensive author relationships with pharmaceutical companies; H. Miao and V. Bunn were Takeda employees, and K. Fenton, M. Fanale, and M. Puhlmann were Seagen employees and shareholders.
De-identified patient-level trial data were offered after study completion on a case-by-case basis to qualified researchers with methodologically sound proposals, subject to internal review.
